label: Grounds of contingent concrete things precede them in time
definition: GroundsPrecedeAt h Concrete grounds v holds when, in history v, whenever y grounds a contingent concrete individual x under the supplied grounding relation at v and x is present at moment t, y is present at some moment strictly earlier than t. In ordinary language: whatever grounds a contingent thing had already been there before each moment at which that thing is present. A thing appearing at time 1, grounded by something present at time 0, satisfies it. So does a thing sustained by a ground present at all times, provided the thing is never present at a moment with nothing earlier; a thing present at an initial moment fails it even with an all-time sustainer (ComingToBeHorns control 4). It fails when some ground has no moment of presence before some moment of the grounded thing: in particular at a moment with nothing earlier, and for a ground present only at the same moments, only later, or never.
note: Analyst formulation; attribution deferred. The grounding relation is the world-relative relation of BruteFoundationBoundary.Profile, not efficient causation of an event, and carries no temporal-presence constraint of its own. So rejecting this principle does not mean simultaneous grounding: a ground may be simultaneous (ComingToBeHorns controls 4 and 5), only later (control 7), or never present. A sustaining (per se) ground that was also present earlier satisfies it; the per se versus temporally prior distinction is the subject of the linked finite-causal-history disambiguation. It constrains every ground, not just one. Applicability OPEN.
